pairs.why: A's ship is turned a little toward the viewer, so more deck and hull curve show, which is nearer the real card's high 3/4 view. B is closer to a flat side profile.
B's truss runs roughly horizontal across the top with mild perspective, as in the real card. A's steep diagonal truss reads as wide-angle.
B is flat-on and frontal with a shallow sill, like the real door. A adds a stoop, lamp, pot and receding tiles, which are extra depth layers the real card lacks.
B's camera sits higher and shows more of the base's top face and the tilted sand plane, closer to the real card's downward look. A looks lower and more side-on.
A's head shows a top face and a bit of turn, and its railing recedes more, which is closer to the real card's slightly high, turned view. B is a flat frontal face.
A's ship is turned slightly more toward the viewer with more visible deck. B is flatter and more side-on with a smaller wave plane.
A's dock is angled so more of the deck's top surface shows. B is symmetric and frontal, further from the real card's high, tilted view.
Both show a similar tilted top view of the device on concentric rings, and neither differs clearly from the real card's camera.
